fact: A giant planet circling Pollux — the first world found around a nearby giant star.
bio: Pollux b (Beta Geminorum b) is a gas giant several times Jupiter's mass orbiting Pollux, the brighter of the mythological Twins and the nearest giant star to the Sun. Confirmed in 2006 from the star's slow wobble, it showed that even evolved giant stars — the Sun's own distant future — can keep massive planets in tow.
